v-la-vague-d-or-cheval-blanc-st-.name: La Vague d'Or — Cheval Blanc St-Tropez
v-la-vague-d-or-cheval-blanc-st-.short: La Vague d'Or — Cheval Blanc St-Tropez
v-la-vague-d-or-cheval-blanc-st-.why: The house is a summer transplant of the Cheval Blanc mothership at the Vendée coast — Bernard Arnault's LVMH hotel arm — dropped onto the Bouillabaisse beach at the very edge of town where the peninsula road first meets the water.
v-la-vague-d-or-cheval-blanc-st-.address: Cheval Blanc St-Tropez, Plage de la Bouillabaisse, 83990 Saint-Tropez, Var, France
v-la-vague-d-or-cheval-blanc-st-.verdict: Three Michelin stars since 2013, held again in the 2026 Guide France — the Var's headline table, where you come for Arnaud Donckele's sauces before anything on the plate.
v-la-vague-d-or-cheval-blanc-st-.signature: The sauces. Donckele is celebrated as a master saucier (Gault&Millau) — his vinaigrettes and marbled herb coulis are built as "a sauce to be eaten," the structure of a dish rather than its finish.
v-la-vague-d-or-cheval-blanc-st-.caveat: Seasonal and stratospheric: Cheval Blanc St-Tropez is a summer-season house, open only from roughly early May to mid-October (the 2026 season runs 7 May–11 October) and dark the rest of the year; this is top-of-market tasting-menu spending — menus from €445 in 2026 — not a casual meal, so book weeks ahead. One correction to the usual line: from the Bouillabaisse beach the terrace faces the Gulf of Saint-Tropez, not the Baie des Canoubiers, which lies on the peninsula's north-east side.

signal_chip.label: 3 Michelin stars
signal_chip.full: Three MICHELIN stars, awarded 2013 and retained in the 2026 Guide France

v-la-vague-d-or-cheval-blanc-st-._lane: The summit — three stars and two

v-la-table-du-castellet.name: La Table du Castellet
v-la-table-du-castellet.address: Hôtel & Spa du Castellet, 3001 Route des Hauts du Camp, 83330 Le Castellet, Var, France
v-la-table-du-castellet.verdict: A three-star built on subtraction, not spectacle: fish or vegetable taken one at a time, each carried by a single full-bodied sauce. Judge it by the encornet à la provençale — flat-cooked squid under a marjoram-scented jus. If that plate doesn't justify the restraint, nothing on the menu will.
v-la-table-du-castellet.signature: Encornet à la provençale: squid cooked slow and flat, laid over chickpeas and finished with a poultry jus perfumed with fresh marjoram — one of Ferré's signature plates.
v-la-table-du-castellet.caveat: Not a village table you stumble into. It's a dining room inside a 5-star resort beside the Circuit Paul Ricard, reached by car, at three-star prices — and the identity is young, reopened only in April 2023. Expect precision and calm, not Provençal rusticity. Coordinates below are approximate to the resort, not the exact door.
v-la-table-du-castellet.person: Fabien Ferré — born 13 Dec 1988 in Autun; arrived at the Hôtel du Castellet in 2013 and rose to be Christophe Bacquié's number two over roughly a decade there, before reopening the restaurant in 2023 and taking three stars in 2024, at 35 — the youngest three-star chef in France.

signal_chip.label: Straight to three stars, 2024
signal_chip.full: Awarded three Michelin stars at once in March 2024 under Fabien Ferré — a jump from unstarred to three in a single ceremony, only the third time in thirty years a French chef has done so, and at 35 the youngest three-star chef in France.

v-la-table-du-castellet._lane: The summit — three stars and two

v-la-voile-la-reserve-de-ramatue.name: La Voile — La Réserve de Ramatuelle
v-la-voile-la-reserve-de-ramatue.short: La Voile — La Réserve de Ramatuelle
v-la-voile-la-reserve-de-ramatue.why: Canino carries the cuisine-minceur line direct from Michel Guérard, the chef who invented the idea of lightness as haute cuisine — training he later sharpened under Guy Martin at Le Grand Véfour.
v-la-voile-la-reserve-de-ramatue.address: Chemin de la Quessine (route de l'Escalet), 83350 Ramatuelle, Var, France
v-la-voile-la-reserve-de-ramatue.verdict: Two Michelin stars (won 2020, held in the 2026 Guide) for a Provençal kitchen that runs on olive oil, garden vegetables and the sea instead of butter — order the rouget poached in seawater and the cooking argues its own case. Falsifiable: it drops from two stars, or the plates arrive rich and heavy rather than featherweight.
v-la-voile-la-reserve-de-ramatue.signature: Rouget poached in seawater with crushed tomato and citrus, finished with a reduction of the fish heads — the dish the house and French food press call emblematic of Canino. The all-vegetable tasting menu, appetiser to dessert, is the other reason regulars come back.
v-la-voile-la-reserve-de-ramatue.caveat: It is the gastronomic table of a five-star resort: terrace-only, seasonal (roughly April–October; the resort reopened 1 May 2026), booked months ahead, and priced to match — a destination splurge, not a discovery. The stars date to 2020; the 2026 Guide confirms retention, not a new promotion. Listed coordinates are approximate to the domain, not the dining room.

signal_chip.label: ★★ Michelin
signal_chip.full: Two MICHELIN Stars, MICHELIN Guide France 2026

v-la-voile-la-reserve-de-ramatue._lane: The summit — three stars and two

v-colette-hotel-sezz.name: Colette — Hôtel Sezz
v-colette-hotel-sezz.why: The restaurant is named for the writer Colette, who kept a small house next door; chef Philippe Colinet sources the whole menu from the market gardeners, fishermen and oyster growers of the gulf.
v-colette-hotel-sezz.address: Hôtel Sezz Saint-Tropez, 151 route des Salins, 83990 Saint-Tropez, Var
v-colette-hotel-sezz.verdict: The one Saint-Tropez grande table where a courgette or a grilled oyster is asked to carry the plate rather than a slab of caviar. Falsifiable test: if the star is pulled, the menu turns meat-heavy, or the room stops running dinner-only, this verdict is wrong. As of the 2026 MICHELIN Guide France it holds one star, Colinet is still in the pass, and the "Originel" menu is genuinely 100% plant-based. Come for restraint and Provençal produce; skip it if you want a red-meat-and-oligarch-wine-list night.
v-colette-hotel-sezz.signature: The house frames two tasting menus. The namesake gesture is the "Originel" — 100% plant-based, vegetables carrying the whole score rather than a garnish; the "Substantiel" alternative is built on the chef's signature dishes (oyster, squid risotto). Plant- and sea-leaning throughout. (These are the house- and tourism-listed signatures, not a single fixed dish.)
v-colette-hotel-sezz.person: Chef Philippe Colinet, Maître Restaurateur — has headed Colette since 2020 and holds its Michelin star (Guide France) from 2021 through the 2026 Guide. Cooks stripped-back, producer-sourced Provençal cuisine drawn from the market gardeners, fishermen and olive and oyster growers of the Gulf of Saint-Tropez. The restaurant is named for the writer Colette, who kept a small house next to the hotel.
v-colette-hotel-sezz.caveat: Grande in every sense: dinner only (roughly 7:30–9:30pm), seasonal — open May 1 to early October in 2026, dark in winter. Multi-act tasting menus about €148–€196 (the act count varies by source, four to seven), plus a chef's table facing the glassed-in pass at a premium. Closed two evenings most weeks — Tue/Wed in the shoulder months (May/June/Sept/Oct) and Mon/Tue in high summer (July/Aug) per the hotel's own listing, so book well ahead. On timing: the chef arrived in 2020 and the restaurant has held its star in the MICHELIN Guide France since 2021. It sits at Hôtel Sezz out on route des Salins, a few minutes east of the village toward Plage des Salins — not in the old port.
v-colette-hotel-sezz.hook: Saint-Tropez's one starred table that lets a vegetable finish the sentence.

signal_chip.label: 1★ MICHELIN
signal_chip.full: One MICHELIN star, Guide France — held since 2021, listed in the 2026 Guide

v-recif-hotel-les-roches-rouges.name: Récif — Hôtel Les Roches Rouges
v-recif-hotel-les-roches-rouges.why: From the rooftop you look straight out at the Île d'Or, the tower-topped islet that locals say gave Hergé the model for Tintin's "Black Island."
v-recif-hotel-les-roches-rouges.address: 90 boulevard de la 36ème Division du Texas, 83530 Saint-Raphaël (Boulouris)
v-recif-hotel-les-roches-rouges.verdict: Falsifiable: it has held one Michelin star every year since 2019 (Guide Michelin) — and, unusually for a kitchen that changed hands, the star carried over. José Bailly won it; Alexandre Baule took the stove in May 2025, and the current Michelin listing already describes his cooking, star intact. What changed is not the rating but the register — the strict no-meat identity is gone.
v-recif-hotel-les-roches-rouges.signature: A vegetable-and-sea register the Michelin Guide now credits to Baule's kitchen: mackerel worked from head to tail, oysters from nearby Tamaris, squid cannelloni (Guide Michelin). Three tasting menus — from a fully plant-based "Tout végétal" through "Hommage à la Méditerranée" to the eight-course "Balade Gourmande" — roughly €150–€210.
v-recif-hotel-les-roches-rouges.caveat: The strict no-meat identity belonged to José Bailly, who won the star in 2019 on vegetables and fish alone. His successor Alexandre Baule (arrived 14 May 2025, from the one-star La Table de l'Alpaga in Megève) puts local meat back on the plate beside the fish and vegetables, and splits his year between here and Megève — so the meat-free promise no longer holds, even though the star has carried into his tenure. Spring–summer only; dinner, Wednesday to Sunday.

signal_chip.label: ★ Michelin
signal_chip.full: One Michelin star, held every year since 2019

v-shanael.name: Shanael
v-shanael.why: Shanael is a contraction of the Denons' children's names; Anthony cooked through Ducasse's Louis XV, Le Meurice and the Plaza Athénée and already held stars at Chantilly and in Paris before betting the family on a Toulon back street.
v-shanael.address: 10 rue Molière, 83000 Toulon (place de l'Opéra, Vieux Toulon)
v-shanael.verdict: Toulon's only Michelin-starred table — and its first in a generation. Denon opened opposite the opera in December 2025 and took the star four months later (Guide Michelin 2026, announced 16 March 2026) — vegetables leading, meat kept in support, sourcing as spine. Not the city's first star ever: Toulon had gone without one since La Chamade (chef Francis Bonneau) closed in 2001. Falsifiable: it is the sole starred restaurant in the city of Toulon, and the star came within a single season of opening.
v-shanael.signature: Artichauts juste saisis — boudin noir, pomme, jus végétal. The artichoke as manifesto: the vegetable carries the plate and the black pudding is kept to a whisper, the clearest read on what Denon means by "vegetables first."
v-shanael.caveat: Not a casual drop-in. A small room of roughly thirty to thirty-six seats (sources differ), so book well ahead. Dinner tasting menus run about €95–165 (weekday lunch from around €49) — a special-occasion table, not a value pick. Prices come from trade press, not the Michelin listing, and moved during 2026, so confirm when reserving.
v-shanael.person: Anthony Denon (Guadeloupean chef; wife Laëtitia Denon runs the dining room — the name Shanael is a contraction of their children's first names). Trained at École hôtelière Médéric; passed through Les Ambassadeurs at the Hôtel de Crillon (under Jean-François Piège and Christophe Saintagne), then Alain Ducasse's Louis XV, Le Meurice and Plaza Athénée; previously earned stars at l'Auberge du Jeu de Paume, Chantilly (2020) and Le Baudelaire, Paris (2022).

signal_chip.label: 1★ Michelin 2026
signal_chip.full: One Michelin star, Guide Michelin France 2026 — announced 16 March 2026, four months after opening; plant-forward cooking backed by short-supply, seasonal sourcing.

v-chez-bruno.name: Chez Bruno
v-chez-bruno.why: The house was built by Clément Bruno — "le pape de la truffe," who died in 2026 — and is now run by his sons Benjamin at the stove and Samuel in the room; its signature is a whole potato baked and buried under grated tuber.
v-chez-bruno.address: 2350 route des Arcs, Campagne Mariette, 83510 Lorgues, Var, France
v-chez-bruno.verdict: A single-obsession pilgrimage: truffle threads every course of the fixed seasonal menu, amuse-bouche to dessert. Falsifiable claim — there is no non-truffle tasting path here (even the vegetarian menu is truffle-built); if you don't love the tuber, this is the wrong temple, and no clever à la carte will save you.
v-chez-bruno.signature: "Le plat d'anthologie de la Maison Bruno" — a whole potato baked in its skin and buried under truffle (truffle cream and freshly grated tuber), the dish the house was built on. It appears on every menu.
v-chez-bruno.person: Benjamin Bruno (kitchen) and Samuel Bruno (dining room) — sons of founder Clément Bruno, "le pape de la truffe" (d. 2026)
v-chez-bruno.caveat: Not cheap and not for the truffle-indifferent. Truffle menus run roughly €98 to €218 before wine (children's menu €25). The black Melanosporum that made the house famous is a winter tuber — come off-season and it gives way to milder varieties (autumn Uncinatum or the white Albidum), a different and lesser thing. It sits in open country off the route des Arcs, not in Lorgues town; hours narrow to Tuesday–Sunday from mid-September to mid-June, so book ahead and check the calendar before you drive out.
v-chez-bruno.hook: A restaurant that serves essentially one ingredient and dares you to fall in love with it — truffle from the first bite to the last, or nothing at all.

signal_chip.label: 1 MICHELIN STAR
signal_chip.full: One Star ('high quality cooking') in the MICHELIN Guide France 2026; the house and regional press report a Michelin star held since 1990.

v-le-faventia-terre-blanche.name: Le Faventia — Terre Blanche
v-le-faventia-terre-blanche.why: Quentin André cut his teeth under Pierre Gagnaire — Les Airelles, Le Balzac, Sketch — before serving as Christophe Schmitt's second here and taking the pass in 2024.
v-le-faventia-terre-blanche.address: Terre Blanche Hôtel Spa Golf Resort, 3100 Route de Bagnols-en-Forêt, 83440 Tourrettes, France
v-le-faventia-terre-blanche.verdict: Order the agneau de Provence — savory-herb crust, candied sweet potato, tart mulberries in a blueberry-cut jus, a dusting of gomasio — or the seven-course Sentiers Méditerranéens (€195), and Quentin André's case for the arrière-pays lands: this is not coastal Riviera gloss but Tourves baby vegetables, Saint-Raphaël line-caught fish and Vidauban poultry cooked with restraint. If the star ever reads as resort-hotel decoration rather than earned, that lamb is where you'll catch the lie — or fail to.
v-le-faventia-terre-blanche.signature: Agneau de Provence — savory-herb crust, candied sweet potato, tart mulberries in a blueberry-cut jus, a whisper of gomasio.
v-le-faventia-terre-blanche.caveat: A five-star golf-resort dining room priced to match: the Sentiers Méditerranéens tasting runs €165 (5 courses) or €195 (7), with a vegetarian Saveurs de Garrigue from €140 — there is no cheap way in. It's a seasonal, dinner-only table: the 2026 season runs late April to 26 October, closed off-season and on the early-week days, so reserve well ahead. It sits up in the pine-forested hills above Fayence, off the coast entirely, not walkable from anywhere.
v-le-faventia-terre-blanche.hook: A one-star that hides up in the pine-forested hills above Fayence, off the coast entirely — the interior Var on a plate. Quentin André, who cut his teeth with Pierre Gagnaire (Les Airelles, Le Balzac, Sketch) before serving as Christophe Schmitt's second, took the pass in 2024 and cooks the hinterland: Tourves baby vegetables, Saint-Raphaël line-caught fish, Vidauban poultry, local cheese.

signal_chip.label: 1★ MICHELIN 2026
signal_chip.full: One MICHELIN star, retained in the 2026 Guide (announced 16 March 2026); first awarded in 2023 under Christophe Schmitt, held under chef Quentin André since 2024.

v-hostellerie-de-l-abbaye-de-la-.name: Hostellerie de l'Abbaye de la Celle
v-hostellerie-de-l-abbaye-de-la-.short: Hostellerie de l'Abbaye de la Celle
v-hostellerie-de-l-abbaye-de-la-.why: Nicolas Pierantoni was raised in La Celle village, joined the inn's 1999 opening team, was sent by Ducasse to train under Franck Cerutti at Monaco's Louis XV, and came home to take the head-chef post in 2016.
v-hostellerie-de-l-abbaye-de-la-.address: 10 Place du General de Gaulle, 83170 La Celle, Var, France
v-hostellerie-de-l-abbaye-de-la-.verdict: Alain Ducasse's 18th-century abbey inn in Provence Verte, where his home-grown protege Nicolas Pierantoni cooks a Provence that mostly walks in from the potager: he sources close to the entire menu locally, much of it from the property's own kitchen garden, working with market gardeners and farmers he speaks to daily.
v-hostellerie-de-l-abbaye-de-la-.signature: Pigeon Mieral, celeris et cerises — pigeon with celeriac and celery branch and fresh cherries, finished with fresh almond and rosemary; a garden-and-orchard plate that shifts with the season.
v-hostellerie-de-l-abbaye-de-la-.person: Nicolas Pierantoni — born in Brignoles, raised in the village of La Celle. He joined the inn's opening team in 1999, was sent by Ducasse to train under executive chef Franck Cerutti at Le Louis XV in Monaco, returned to La Celle in 2006 as sous-chef to Benoit Witz, and was named head chef by Alain Ducasse in 2016 when Witz left.
v-hostellerie-de-l-abbaye-de-la-.caveat: No current Michelin star, told straight: the inn held one star from 2006 until the 2024 guide, when it was the only Var restaurant to lose its star — Michelin now lists it 'Restaurant selectionne 2026', no star. The standing distinction is Gault&Millau's 2 toques (13/20, 2026). Add gastronomic Ducasse-group pricing (roughly EUR 124 average a la carte), a ten-room inn deep in the Var countryside, a menu chained to the garden and the season, and an annual January-to-mid-February closure — book well ahead.
v-hostellerie-de-l-abbaye-de-la-.hook: The abbey inn where Ducasse keeps a thirty-kilometre pantry.
v-hostellerie-de-l-abbaye-de-la-._lane: The hinterland houses — the truffle, the garden, the abbey

v-club-55.name: Club 55
v-club-55.why: It began as a wooden shack with no electricity; to feed the film crew in 1955 Geneviève de Colmont borrowed a Saint-Tropez baker's oven to roast the beef, and the family creed is still that the guest is not a king but a friend.
v-club-55.address: 43 Boulevard Patch, Plage de Pampelonne, 83350 Ramatuelle, Var (Côte d'Azur), France
v-club-55.verdict: Come for the myth, not the Michelin — there is no star here and never has been. The kitchen does one thing well: unfussy Provençal built on its own farm — the raw-vegetable basket, a whole grilled sea bass, a strawberry tart. Judge it as gastronomy and you leave disappointed and lighter of wallet; judge it as the first restaurant on Pampelonne, still run by the family that fed Bardot's crew in 1955, and it is the one table on this coast worth the trip for the place alone.
v-club-55.signature: Le panier de crudités — a whole basket of raw garden vegetables with hard-boiled eggs and a mayonnaise dip, drawn from the family's own farm (Ferme des Bouis, Ramatuelle).
v-club-55.person: Owner and host is Camille de Colmont, who took over the family business after her father Patrice de Colmont died on 11 October 2025, aged 77 (her mother Corinne and aunt Véronique remain in the business). Laurent Bertolotto is the long-serving kitchen chef — a 2021 profile put his tenure at 28 years cooking his grandmother's Provençal recipes — but his current 2026 status is unconfirmed (recent transition coverage names only "a solid kitchen team", not him), so treat him as long-standing-but-possibly-former, not a verified 2026 chef.
v-club-55.caveat: Ruinously priced and unapologetic about it — a whole fish, a rosé and two crudité baskets vanish into three figures fast, and sunbeds/parking are billed apart; it trades on scene as much as cooking. Seasonal: the 2026 season runs 27 March–1 November (shut in winter), and it heaves in July–August — reserve well ahead and expect no walk-in miracle. Lat/lng is approximate to the beach frontage.
v-club-55.hook: The wooden shack that fed Brigitte Bardot's film crew in 1955 became the first club on Pampelonne — and still runs on the house creed that the guest is not a king but a friend.

signal_chip.label: BORN 1955 — BARDOT
signal_chip.full: The first restaurant on Pampelonne, begun as the wooden-shack canteen feeding the cast and crew of Roger Vadim's 'Et Dieu créa la femme' (And God Created Woman, released 1956), Brigitte Bardot among them. No Michelin star then or now — the standing is cultural, not gastronomic.
signal_chip.cosign: Brigitte Bardot & Roger Vadim, 'Et Dieu créa la femme' (1956); de Colmont family, founders (1955)

v-club-55._lane: On the sand — Pampelonne and the islands

v-la-plage-d-argent.name: La Plage d'Argent
v-la-plage-d-argent.neighborhood: Plage d'Argent, Ile de Porquerolles (Iles d'Hyeres / Iles d'Or)
v-la-plage-d-argent.why: Porquerolles is the largest of the Iles d'Or, a national park you reach by boat and cross by bicycle. Verified: La Plage d'Argent has been a family institution on its namesake beach since 1957, opening seasonally from about mid-April to the end of September.
v-la-plage-d-argent.address: Plage d'Argent, Ile de Porquerolles, 83400 Hyeres
v-la-plage-d-argent.verdict: The Le Ber family has held this pine-backed beach restaurant since 1957, a true Iles d'Or institution reached only on foot or by bike through the national park. Honest: it is a beach table (grills, tartares, salads) at island prices, and reviews swing with the day, so come for the setting and the plancha, not for gastronomy. Falsifiable: seasonal, roughly mid-April to end-September, closed Mondays; mostly daytime, with dinner on Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday evenings in July-August.
v-la-plage-d-argent.signature: The grilled catch of the day off the plancha, in the pine shade; the fish and the view are the entire argument.
v-la-plage-d-argent.caveat: Seasonal and largely a daytime table (dinner only on select July-August evenings), weather-dependent. No cars on the island, so it is a walk or bike ride from the port, and island prices apply.
v-la-plage-d-argent.hook: Grilled fish under the maritime pines on the one Porquerolles beach the islanders still treat as their own, run by the same family since 1957.

v-le-mas-du-langoustier.name: Le Mas du Langoustier
tags: Michelin Guide-listed island table — grilled langouste and whole fish to share
productTags: Michelin Guide-listed island table — grilled langouste and whole fish to share
v-le-mas-du-langoustier.why: The mas is the old estate house of Porquerolles' western tip, an outpost of the Sainte-Anne domain at the end of a pine track the estate still keeps private.
v-le-mas-du-langoustier.address: Le Mas du Langoustier, Pointe du Langoustier, 83400 Île de Porquerolles, Hyères, Var, France
v-le-mas-du-langoustier.subcat: Michelin Guide-listed island table — grilled langouste and whole fish to share
v-le-mas-du-langoustier.verdict: Its terrace, La Pinède, sits at the estate's western point on Porquerolles, reached only by the hotel's land shuttle from the port after the ferry. The house specialty is a whole grilled langouste or a whole grilled fish, brought out to be shared with family or friends. Open 24 April to 27 September 2026: lunch 12h15–14h00 (reservation recommended), dinner by reservation only.
v-le-mas-du-langoustier.signature: A whole grilled langouste (spiny lobster) or a whole grilled fish, carried to the pine terrace to be shared with family or friends — the house's signature.
v-le-mas-du-langoustier.caveat: Strictly seasonal and remote: closed roughly October to late April (2026 window 24 April–27 September) and reachable only by the hotel's land shuttle from the port — confirm dates and book before you cross. La Pinède is the bistronomic terrace (Gault&Millau 12/20 'Table Gourmande'); it serves lunch and, by reservation only, dinner. The estate's former gastronomic room is not the same table and its status has been reported as uncertain.

signal_chip.label: In the Michelin Guide
signal_chip.full: In the 2026 Michelin Guide selection as La Pinède, Le Mas du Langoustier; also Gault&Millau 12/20, rated a 'Table Gourmande.'
